scope: Known videos used for tuning/regression, not held-out accuracy measurement.

geometric_regression.scope: Simplified skeleton with known torso orientation and flattened arm depth, not field accuracy.

new_video_review.scope: Human intervals and order are review-only, not runtime inputs or independent accuracy.

program_changes: Per-person forearm projection scale from bounded high-quality observations; no model training or extra inference.
Compete both possible depth signs against body front/side directions, plus bounded contraction evidence after a separately stable lateral endpoint.
Maintain independent contiguous forward votes rather than overwriting preparatory lateral votes; bounded wait resolves a stronger flat-depth side label one frame earlier.
Require a real new pose and retain lowering, bimanual, weak-walking, body-turn and missing-reference suppression.
Scale the voting window to the full required duration, fixing impossible compact/inferred front confirmation at high FPS.
known_remaining_errors: Real-video gain is limited: 21_14_58 forward 19 to 20, left/right remain 24/22. Human review has 29 of each; 5 left, 7 right and 9 forward still missing.

Synthetic 22 angle/start-side cases confirm forward v8=4, v9=18. These assume correct torso orientation and are not field accuracy. Four ±45-degree ambiguous cases still miss front, and the original body rule can mislabel a side.
If torso heading and arm depth both fail, projection compensation remains ambiguous. Weak depth without a prior stable pointing endpoint is not independently labeled forward by this supplement.
13 and 16 still miss right; 3 retains some direction errors, including dominant F1/L0/R1 on L/R-only footage and a background forward false confirmation.
